Where credits get stuck

A returned part is not the same as an applied credit.

Core and return paperwork can pass through the service counter, parts room, shop system, vendor portal, and monthly statement. One missed handoff can leave a valid credit sitting unresolved.

01

Part returned

The core or unused part leaves the shop, often with a receipt, tag, or pickup record.

02

Credit issued

The vendor creates a credit memo, but the amount or reference may not line up with the shop record.

03

Statement applied

The credit must land on the right vendor account and statement before the loop is truly closed.

Common questions

Know exactly what the pilot does.

Is this bookkeeping or accounting?

No. This is a limited parts-credit reconciliation. We identify and document matches and exceptions. Your shop or accountant remains responsible for accounting entries.

Do you need access to our shop software?

No. We work from the vendor statements and repair-order exports you provide. We do not ask for bank credentials or full accounting access.

Will you contact our vendors?

Only after you review the findings and approve the specific items. You stay in control of every vendor conversation.

Do you guarantee every flagged credit will be recovered?

No. A flagged item is a documented exception that needs vendor confirmation. Recovery depends on vendor records, return terms, timing, and available proof.

What if the records are messy?

That is common. Send what you have. We will tell you what can be matched, what is missing, and whether the pilot can proceed before the review starts.
